proposed_statement_changes.reason: The negative deficiency bound is correct, but the former final sentence called exact observation of \(b\) a valid limit without specifying the comparison metric. That wording could be read as a two-sided total-variation or Le Cam equivalence, which is false for a continuously varying \(b\). The replacement retains the obstruction and narrows the positive transfer claim to the uniform weak-risk conclusion actually implied by the joint Gaussian approximation and uniform consistency of \((\widehat b_{j,n})_{j\in\mathcal J}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The existing construction asks for two-sided Markov-kernel equivalence to exact observation of a continuously varying unscaled effect. Consistency of \((\widehat b_{j,n})_{j\in\mathcal J}\) gives weak convergence and bounded uniformly equicontinuous risk convergence, but not total-variation recovery of the point mass \(\delta_b\). The replacement records the valid direct risk route and exposes the additional conditions needed by unbounded diameter and discontinuous coverage losses.

The narrowed statement introduces the score-only covariance and observation and the reduced-law expectation explicitly, so its symbol-dependency metadata must be synchronized with the corrected claim.

The comparator metadata must distinguish the proved bounded uniformly equicontinuous risk transfer from the rejected two-sided deficiency claim and point the three transfer comparisons to the theorem that establishes the obstruction and qualified replacement.

proposed.comparator_claim: Argmax-winner inference motivates separating honest projection from oracle behavior, but its selection rule and estimand differ from the exact-zero donor-face model.
Expected-measure confidence-set duality is only a template unless domination, product measurability, and a reduction from fixed-measure loss to diameter are proved for donor faces.
Simultaneous inference motivates universal post-selection validity, not minimax optimality of the maximum-critical donor hull.

Weak-identification subsequence methods motivate uniformity analysis but do not supply two-sided deficiency equivalence to exact observation of a continuously varying unscaled effect; the present theorem instead proves bounded uniformly equicontinuous risk transfer directly.

Conditional Gaussian inference motivates identification-robust calibration but does not remove the effect-coordinate scaling obstruction; the qualified score-only risk comparison is proved directly here.
Few-treated-group inference with many controls is distinct from inference driven by many micro observations within a fixed finite set of labels.
Time-series synthetic-control inference is distinct from exact-score donor-label uncertainty in fixed-label micro-panels.

Global two-sided asymptotic equivalence is not delivered by the panel moment assumptions and is quantitatively ruled out for the frozen fixed-noise effect experiment; only the direct qualified risk comparison is retained.

prose_updates.tldr: A finite menu of prespecified donor stacks creates nonregular inference when validity is defined by an exact zero of a noisy baseline score. The panel procedures remain causal only under the explicit nonempty exact-close and shared-slope additive untreated-change conditions; zero score alone does not imply target coherence in the abstract Gaussian limit. The unrestricted-effect full Gaussian frontier is infinite. The finite bounded-spread repair is a score-only first-order decision benchmark: it observes \(b\) exactly and retains Gaussian noise only in root-sample-scaled scores. Its two-state value is \(\Delta[\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha]_+\), with zero-diameter elbow \(\rho=2z_{1-\alpha}\), and a simultaneous score-screen hull bounds the general value by \(B\). The reduced panel statistic converges uniformly to this score-only law for bounded uniformly equicontinuous risk payoffs, but no two-sided Le Cam equivalence to exact observation of a continuously varying \(b\) is claimed. None of these conditional results validates the historical CMS comparison-state estimates.

project_justification.gap: Existing few-treated panel and synthetic-control methods do not solve honest expected-diameter inference when a valid donor label is defined by an exact zero score and several labels may lie on the same face. Generic post-selection results also do not determine the minimax constant for this discontinuous target map or justify replacing a consistent unscaled effect estimate by exact observation in two-sided deficiency.
project_justification.niche: The CMS comparison-state workflow has finitely many candidate labels, many beneficiaries within each state, unequal sample sizes, reused controls, and uncertainty about exact transport. A causal conclusion requires an exact population equality plus a model connecting the score to untreated changes. Ranked empirical balance supplies neither, and the abstract implication from zero scores to a common effect is an additional restriction rather than an algebraic fact.
project_justification.fill: The project proves exact-close transport under the explicit shared-slope untreated-change model, gives uniformly honest simultaneous and pilot-adaptive procedures with fixed-separation oracle behavior, proves that the full fixed-noise Gaussian frontier is infinite when effect spread is unrestricted, and supplies the bounded-spread score-only repair. The repaired experiment has an exact two-state Mahalanobis minimax formula, a general embedded-pair lower bound, and a simultaneous-screen upper bound \(B\). The finite-sample reduced statistic admits a direct uniform risk transfer for bounded uniformly equicontinuous payoffs; exact general finite-face minimaxity, unbounded-diameter transfer without an added uniform-integrability condition, and two-sided deficiency equivalence to exact observation are not claimed.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Group means and within-group covariance matrices are estimated directly, and the known contrast matrix propagates covariance from shared treated groups and reused controls. Spectral clipping totalizes the feasible panel inversions. In the first-order local decision benchmark, only the root-sample-scaled score vector has Gaussian noise and the unscaled donor-effect vector is treated as exactly observed because its estimation error is \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). This yields direct transfer for bounded uniformly equicontinuous risks, not total-variation or two-sided deficiency equivalence to a point mass at continuously varying \(b\).

prose_updates.related_work: The reviewed RTI material describes the CMS comparison-state workflow through ranked baseline distance, retained comparison states, claims-driven substitutions, and person-level weighting; it does not document ex ante algebraic calibration to known population totals for every score component. Hence the workflow is a motivating and falsifiable use case, not evidence that the paper's exact-close assumptions held historically. Conley and Taber and Ferman and Pinto obtain reference variation from many control groups, unlike the many-within-group, fixed-label regime here. Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu study time-series synthetic-control inference rather than exact donor-face uncertainty. Berk et al. motivate simultaneous protection but do not establish minimaxity of the maximum-critical hull. Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey study argmax-winner selection; the present exact-zero-face model is not their argmax-selection model, and neither parameter class contains the other without changing both the selection rule and the estimand. Their work motivates the separate pilot-adaptive oracle construction only. Evans, Hansen, and Stark supply an acceptance-region expected-measure template, but their duality is not used as a theorem here because domination, product measurability, and the reduction from fixed sigma-finite expected measure to expected diameter have not been proved. Andrews and Cheng, Andrews and Mikusheva, and Nussbaum motivate weak-limit and experiment-comparison questions but do not remove the effect-coordinate scaling obstruction. The present theorem derives only the supported direct transfer for bounded uniformly equicontinuous risk payoffs and quantitatively rejects the frozen two-sided deficiency comparison.
prose_updates.interpretation: The infinite full Gaussian frontier is an ill-posedness diagnosis, not a failure of simultaneous panel coverage: with unrestricted \(b\), nearly indistinguishable score faces can select effects separated by arbitrarily large \(\Delta\). The bounded score-only experiment isolates the weak-separation cost after ordinary unscaled post-mean noise vanishes. Exact observation of \(b\) is therefore a first-order decision-risk benchmark, not a total-variation representation of the finite-sample estimate. Exact two-face adaptation is governed by Mahalanobis score separation, while a covariance-aware simultaneous screen remains valid on multiple-zero faces. For the CMS workflow, the operational implication is to prespecify and audit exact calibration and untreated-trend transport; good ranked balance cannot be substituted for either condition.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The unrestricted-effect full Gaussian benchmark has minimax expected diameter \(+\infty\), so no finite general program can attain it. The repaired score-only bounded-spread experiment has an exact two-state value and the finite general bound \(0\leq\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)\leq B\), including shared-control covariance and multiple-zero faces, but its exact general-\(J\) constant is not derived. Evans--Hansen--Stark duality remains only a template because the necessary domination, joint measurability, and expected-measure-to-diameter reduction are absent. For the panel-to-score-only step, the reduced statistic is uniformly close only in the weak topology under the stated assumptions. This suffices for bounded uniformly equicontinuous risk payoffs. Unbounded expected diameter additionally needs uniform integrability, discontinuous coverage needs boundary control, and two-sided Le Cam deficiency equivalence to exact observation of continuously varying \(b\) is false. The accepted pilot-adaptive construction and its oracle-equivalence statement are unchanged.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Uniform causal coverage and fixed-separation oracle conclusions apply only to the triangular-array panel class satisfying consistency, stable group fractions, moment and covariance regularity, a nonempty exact close set, and the shared-slope additive untreated-change condition. In the abstract Gaussian face problems, equality of the \(b_j\) values at simultaneous zero-score labels is separately imposed and is not implied by \(h_j=0\). The original unrestricted-effect full Gaussian frontier is infinite. Finite weak-separation risk statements concern the bounded-spread score-only experiment with exactly observed \(b\), positive definite \(\Gamma\), and spread at most \(B\). The exact theorem covers any two embedded faces and the simultaneous screen covers general finite faces, while the finite-sample transfer proved here is limited to bounded uniformly equicontinuous payoffs. Exact general-face minimaxity, unbounded-diameter transfer without uniform integrability, discontinuous-coverage transfer without boundary control, and two-sided deficiency equivalence to exact observation are not claimed. No reviewed source establishes the exact calibration assumptions for the historical CMS estimates.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem separates two notions that the former transfer recipe conflated: the unscaled effect estimate consistently reveals \(b\), which rules out equivalence to a Gaussian experiment with fixed effect-coordinate noise, while uniform weak convergence still transfers bounded uniformly equicontinuous risk payoffs to the exact-\(b\) score-only benchmark.
statement_notes.gap: No parameter-free kernel can turn a noisy estimate of a continuously varying \(b\) into the exact point mass \(\delta_b\) uniformly in total variation. The proved replacement is direct weak-risk convergence; unbounded diameter and discontinuous coverage require additional tail and boundary arguments.
statement_notes.consumer: Use the score-only frontier as a first-order decision-risk benchmark and preserve shared-control score covariance. Do not cite it as a global two-sided Le Cam equivalence or as a finite-sample exact observation result.
